clue.text: Fat people's chins, perhaps, seen in cinema programmes

definitions.meaning: double chins are the extra fleshy features below a heavy jaw
a bill showing two films one after the other for one ticket

explanation.definitionFit: Two films on one bill make a two-film show, and a double chin is a doubled facial feature.

clue.text: Awfully odd duck, a kind of bird you'll never see

definitions.text: a kind of bird you'll never see

indicators.note: awfully suggests the letters of odd are mangled into a new order

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: An oddly behaving duck is described as some bird nobody will ever spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' rearranges ODD to DOD; the cricket duck, a score of zero, gives O.
explanation.definitionFit: The flightless Mauritius bird is extinct, so no living person will ever observe one.

clue.text: Eclipse's finished phase

parts.note: time is up when it is finished
a phase is a stage in a process

explanation.surface: An astronomer notes that an eclipse has reached its final phase.
explanation.definitionFit: To outshine someone or steal their limelight is to eclipse them.

clue.text: Nothing overturns Her Majesty's Ship

indicators.note: overturns in a down clue means the word for nothing is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: nil means nothing, zero
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: Something capsizes a Royal Navy vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocean liner is a large passenger ship.

clue.text: Cost brought down, perhaps

definitions.meaning: an item that sold for a price is said to have made that much at auction
to go and get something, as from upstairs, carrying it down

explanation.definitionFit: A painting that made a high price at sale went for that sum; a dog retrieving a stick brought it back.

clue.text: Getting away from a heartless situation, say, smashed cane

parts.note: a void is an empty space, a situation with nothing at its centre

indicators.note: smashed suggests the word cane is broken up and its letters reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone escapes a bleak, empty state of affairs after breaking a cane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smashed' rearranges CANE to ANCE. The definition is a noun phrase: avoidance is the act of getting away from something.
explanation.definitionFit: Evasion or keeping clear of something is what the noun describes.

clue.text: Regular Army outfit

explanation.definitionFit: Even and consistent things are the same throughout, and soldiers wear standard matching dress.

clue.text: Person presiding over event announced medal

indicators.note: announced means the letters for the medal are spoken aloud

parts.note: MC is the Military Cross, a British gallantry medal

explanation.surface: An official in charge of a ceremony reveals who has won a medal.
explanation.walkthrough: Saying the letters M and C aloud gives the spelt-out form; MC is also master of ceremonies.
explanation.definitionFit: A master of ceremonies hosts and runs a show or function.

clue.text: Remaining child, more likely than not

parts.note: the odd one is the one remaining when the others are paired off
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A leftover child is probably going to be the favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: In betting, a horse at short odds is expected to win, so the term means probable.

clue.text: Not restricted to a single part such as Henry IV

definitions.text: Not restricted to a single part such as Henry IV

parts.words: Not restricted to a single part such as Henry IV
parts.note: Shakespeare's Henry IV comes in Part 1 and Part 2, so it is a play in a pair of portions, like a suit or swimsuit

explanation.surface: A theatre note says the history play cannot be staged as a single evening.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase normally means a suit or bikini; here it describes Shakespeare's history play written in two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Made of a pair of portions, as a bikini or suit is, and as that history play is.

clue.text: Getting thoughtlessly excited is doubly hard on artist

indicators.note: doubly says the combination is repeated once more
on in an across clue places hard after artist

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A painter who is a bit too keen is said to be twice as tough.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes mindless cheerleading enthusiasm, the noisy uncritical support of fans.

clue.text: Renovate old set in port

indicators.note: set in means the abbreviation for old is placed within the port

parts.note: Dover is the English Channel port in Kent

explanation.surface: Instructions to refurbish an antique set in a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: To redecorate or refurbish a room is to give it a fresh makeover.

clue.text: Concealed barrier's height? Eureka!

parts.note: eureka and aha are both cries of discovery

explanation.surface: Someone discovers how tall a hidden fence is and cries out in triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: A ha-ha is a ditch with a sunken wall, used on English country estates to keep livestock out without spoiling the view.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a sunken fence set in a ditch so it cannot be seen from the house.

clue.text: Ordered gin, finally — same again — in European resort

indicators.note: same again says the combination just built is repeated

parts.note: bade is an old past tense of bid, meaning ordered

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of gin

explanation.surface: A drinker orders gin and, at the end, the same again while at a spa.
explanation.definitionFit: A German spa town in the Black Forest, famous as a fashionable watering place.

clue.text: Comic novelist introduces Jack, performing for playwright

indicators.note: introduces means the novelist takes other letters into his middle

parts.note: E F Benson wrote the comic Mapp and Lucia novels
J is the card abbreviation for jack
on means performing, on stage

explanation.surface: A humorous author brings in a sailor who is acting, for a dramatist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introduces' has the novelist's name take in J and ON. E F Benson is best known for the Mapp and Lucia books.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacobean dramatist who wrote Volpone and The Alchemist.

clue.text: Operatic heroine's tailless parrot

indicators.note: tailless says the final letter of the synonym is cut off

parts.note: to parrot is to copy, imitate

explanation.surface: A diva's pet bird has lost its tail feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: The consumptive seamstress who is the heroine of Puccini's La Boheme.

clue.text: The "mater" part of "alma mater"

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Latin lesson points out which bit of the phrase for an old school means mother.
explanation.walkthrough: Mater is Latin for mother, still used in old-fashioned English; the run ALMA MATER holds it across the join.
explanation.definitionFit: Mater is old-fashioned English slang for one's mother, and so is the nursery word.

clue.text: One in 100,000 in India is secular

annotationWithheld.why: One in 100,000 in India is secular (4): I in LAC (100,000 in India); the only leaf for LAC, '100,000 in India', opens with 'in' after letter-less '100,000', which the own-indicator-in-leaf check reads as the container's own indicator, and dropping 'in India' is refused
annotationWithheld.clue: One in 100,000 in India is secular

clue.text: Strip in exotic act for this?

definitions.text: Strip in exotic act for this?

indicators.note: in puts the word for strip inside the reworked act
exotic suggests the letters of act are rearranged in unusual fashion

parts.note: to bare is to strip

explanation.surface: A striptease as part of an exotic routine suggests a certain kind of nightclub show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' rearranges ACT to CAT, which takes in BARE. The whole clue also defines: a strip act is the sort of thing seen at that venue.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightclub entertainment with songs and dancing, sometimes risque.

clue.text: Voltaire, for one, in a term of French

definitions.text: Voltaire, for one, in a term of French

parts.words: Voltaire, for one, in a term of French
parts.note: Voltaire was the assumed writing name of Francois-Marie Arouet, and the phrase for such a name is borrowed from French

explanation.surface: A note on the French philosopher Voltaire and a French expression.
explanation.walkthrough: Voltaire is a pseudonym; the expression for an author's assumed name is French in form.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen name is an assumed name that an author writes under.

clue.text: Killer charged in Spain

parts.note: reads as an arrested murderer, but describes the bullfighter who is charged by the bull in Spanish rings

explanation.surface: A news report that a murderer has been charged by Spanish police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charged' suggests a court; in fact the bull charges this killer.
explanation.definitionFit: The bullfighter who kills the bull in a Spanish corrida.

clue.text: Italian dish Alan cooked with gas

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters of the two words are mixed and reworked

explanation.surface: Alan makes a pasta dish on a gas hob.
explanation.definitionFit: Layered pasta sheets baked with sauce and cheese, a classic Italian dish.

clue.text: Repeatedly show disapproval of mistake

indicators.note: repeatedly says the word for jeering is given twice

parts.note: to boo is to jeer, show disapproval

explanation.surface: Keep jeering at an error.
explanation.definitionFit: A blunder or silly slip, in informal speech.

clue.text: You might see a cone when it's stormy

definitions.text: You might see a cone when it's stormy

indicators.note: stormy suggests the letters of a cone are tossed about

explanation.surface: Coastguards hoist a warning cone when gales are expected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stormy' rearranges A CONE; the whole clue is also the definition, since a storm cone may be raised at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea, where warning cones are hoisted and big waves rise in a storm.

clue.text: Fly as part of jet set, separately

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An insect is said to be part of the wealthy travelling elite, kept apart.
explanation.definitionFit: An African biting insect that spreads sleeping sickness.

clue.text: Finish, as poker players aim to do

definitions.text: as poker players aim to do
definitions.meaning: a card player hopes to be ahead, with more than they started with

explanation.definitionFit: To land up at last somewhere; a gambler wants to come out ahead in winnings.

clue.text: River goddess

definitions.meaning: the Oxford stretch of the Thames is called by this name
the Egyptian goddess of motherhood, wife of Osiris

explanation.definitionFit: The Thames at Oxford is so named, as is the chief Egyptian mother deity.

clue.text: Revisited theme with piano, right? Is framed by wind instrument

indicators.note: framed by means the instrument surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: a reed is a wind instrument, or its vibrating part
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A musician asks whether a returning melody played softly is surrounded by woodwind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'framed by' has REED surround P, R and IS. 'Revisited theme' is a verb phrase: a theme was revisited, as reprised.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, a melody repeated later in a piece has been restated.

clue.text: Make short work of getting archaeological site established

parts.note: a dig is an excavation site

explanation.surface: A team quickly sets up an excavation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make short work of' looks like 'finish fast'; here it means abridge, cut down to a summary.
explanation.definitionFit: To summarise or condense a text is to abridge it into a shorter version.

clue.text: They show, possibly, transient drama

parts.note: television repeats immediately the brief exciting moment in a sporting event, a fleeting piece of action shown again

explanation.surface: A remark that short-lived theatre is staged.
explanation.walkthrough: Transient means instant; drama replayed on screen is a replay.
explanation.definitionFit: Televised sport re-runs a moment just after it happens, for viewers to see again.
